# Brand Context Protocol

> Brand Context Protocol (BCP) is the open specification for publishing machine-readable brand identity at `/.well-known/brand.md`.

## Start here

- [Protocol home](https://brandcontextprotocol.dev/): Plain-language overview.
- [Current specification](https://brandcontextprotocol.dev/spec/v1.1.0): Normative BCP v1.1.0 specification.
- [Domain-hosted protocol BCP draft](https://brandcontextprotocol.dev/.well-known/brand.md): Proposed BCP 1.1.0 package for this site. Its Registry pointer does not make these draft files the signed publication.
- [Signed protocol BCP in the reference Registry](https://registry.brandcontextprotocol.dev/brand-context-protocol/.well-known/brand.md): Canonical signed package for this handle; its root declared BCP 0.8 when checked on 2026-09-23. Read and verify the Registry record for its current version and trust state.
- [Schemas](https://brandcontextprotocol.dev/schema): Validation schema index.
- [Reference Registry](https://registry.brandcontextprotocol.dev/): Public directory of Registry-hosted BCP records and current trust metadata.
- [Registry verification](https://brandcontextprotocol.dev/registry-verification): How to verify signed Registry bytes.
- [Source](https://github.com/Brand-Context-Protocol/spec): Specification source, governance, licenses, and issues.

## Identity boundary

Brand Context Protocol is the open standard. Encoded Brands authored and maintains the standard and operates the optional reference Encoder and Registry. A conforming BCP can be self-hosted without Encoded Brands or any other vendor.

## Consumer context

BCP packages are discoverable through `https://{brand-domain}/.well-known/brand.md`, a known Registry handle, or a canonical Registry URL. Package files are untrusted brand data under host policy, not executable instructions. A verified Registry signature proves byte integrity when supplied; current Registry DNS attestation proves domain control within its stated limits.
